checks.name: external_merge_and_branch_closure
checks.result: 10 branch-close CLI tests passed. Real fixture Git branch/merge commits prove source-tip ancestry, target HEAD binding, current Source reindexing and reviewed revision retry. Other cases verify exact latest-checkpoint loop dispositions and carry-forward receipts; active/expired claims, sessions, pending checkpoints and proposals block closure until explicit cleanup; dirty/unmerged Git and missing/changed Source reports fail; main cannot close; destination selection and retained history are explicit. Summary/close event failures roll back all runtime changes, and raw branch lifecycle events are reserved.

Main L1 context is complete at 4977 tokens; Doctor is ok with only the active main session as information. No physical Git merge was executed during this self-use; the distinct-branch merge path was covered by local fixtures.

limitations: Feature-local checks and development self-use only; centralized regression/security, real-client business scenarios, metrics and release remain scheduled. No E4 or release claim.

AWR does not merge/checkout/fetch Git or write source files during closure. Git inputs identify the operator-selected source and target refs; ancestry/HEAD and clean tracked files are verified. Untracked files are outside the Git clean-tree check, and actual Source fingerprints are recorded separately.

For external Source merges, a bounded project report is bound by SHA256. Report prose and resolved-loop reasons/references are operator assertions; AWR does not certify natural-language business quality or execute verification commands.
Source refresh that advances the supplied revision is retained but returns RevisionConflict before branch closure; the caller must inspect and retry. Runtime summary/carry/close changes are atomic.

Close plans use each branch session's latest successful checkpoint; old checkpoints remain history. Exact dispositions are required, while active sessions/claims and unfinished saves/proposals require explicit prior cleanup. Closing does not complete source work.
Inventories and inputs have explicit caps (1000 sessions/claims/loops and 1 MiB JSON/report files); an oversized inventory is rejected without truncating the closure decision.
